newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - Administaff, Kilroy jump.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - Administaff, Kilroy jump.

text.p: Shares of Texas-based Administaff and real estate investment trust Kilroy surged after their initial public offerings on Wednesday.
Administaff Inc shares jumped 4-7/8 or nearly 30 percent to 21-7/8 in heavy trading. The company was one of the most active issues on the New York Stock Exchange.

Administaff provides adminstrative services like payroll, benefits, and human resources to small businesses. About 80 percent of its revenues are generated in its home state of Texas. It posted net income of $1.1 million on 1995 revenues of $716 million, according to its prospectus.
The three million shares were priced at $17 a share, at the top end of their estimated pricing range of $15 to $17, according to lead underwriter Morgan Stanley.
The pricing range was lifted late yesterday from a previous estimate of $13 to $15.

Kilroy Realty Corp shares jumped about 10 percent, rising 2-3/8 to 25-3/8 on their first day of trading. It was also one of the 10 most active stocks on the NYSE with over three million shares traded at late morning.

Prudential said it priced Kilroy at $23, at the top of its pricing range, after boosting both the number of shares and the price for a share. The number of shares was raised to 12.5 million from its initial estimate of 11.3 million shares. The range was lifted to $22 to $23 from the first estimated range of $19 to $21, it said.
The real estate investment trust is based in El Segundo, California.
Analysts had expected both deals to reap premiums.
Other companies that made their IPO debuts:
-- Coldwater Creek Inc also had a splashy debut. Shares rose 2-1/4 to 17-1/4. Sandpoint, Idaho-based Coldwater is a direct mail retailer of apparel, gifts and jewelry.
-- AmerUs Life Holdings Inc shares jumped 3 to $19.50 each from their IPO price of $16.50.

The company is the holding company for AmerUS Life and is based in Des Moines, Iowa. It offered nearly 4.7 million shares, up from a previous estimate of 3.9 million shares in the offering, led by Goldman Sachs & Co.
Since 1991, AmerUS has been profitable on an annual basis.

-- Medirisk Inc shares fell slightly after the IPO debut of the database and decision-support software company. Shares slipped 1/2 to 10-1/2. Its shares priced at the low end of its estimated range of $11 to $13.
-- Photoelectron Corp shares were flat at $8.50 in midday trading. Shares of the company were priced at $8.50 each, below their range of $9 to $10 each.
-- Template Software Inc shares rose 1/2 to 16-1/2.
